newsitem.title: USA: Oseberg delivery on Feb NYMEX seen lifting WTI.
newsitem.headline: Oseberg delivery on Feb NYMEX seen lifting WTI.

text.p: Norwegian Oseberg crude will be delivered into the expired February NYMEX contract, a rare event which is expected to lift the price of benchmark West Texas Intermediate/Cushing relative to other grades, traders said Tuesday.
"This is the first time (Oseberg has been delivered) in a couple of years, so it'll have a big impact on the cash market," said one Gulf Coast trader.

The degree of impact will depend on the amount of Oseberg being delivered but it is expected that the buyers would look to avoid taking delivery of the crude. The seller is Norway's state oil company Den norske stats oljeselskap AS (Statoil) STAT.CN, traders said, though Statoil traders couldn't be reached for comment.
"This would put a premium on WTI/Cushing EFPs (exchange for physicals)," another trader said, referring to the facility traders have on NYMEX to trade out of physical positions.
Under the contract specifications, the seller can deliver Oseberg on the NYMEX crude contract at a discount of around 30 cents a barrel to the benchmark WTI.
WTI is a lighter crude, with an API gravity of 43.6 degrees compared with 36 degrees for Oseberg, and has a lower sulphur content, which is preferred by most refiners.
